key_insight: AdsNet predicts adsorption energies directly from a local, geometry-sensitive graph rather than modeling the entire surface system.
engineering_relevance: Its local formulation supports efficient catalyst screening and interface relaxation without scaling graph size with the full simulation cell.
method: Build a cutoff-based graph of adsorbate atoms and nearby surface atoms.
Use equivariant message passing with scalar and vector features to predict energy and per-atom contributions.
Compute forces by automatic differentiation for projected-gradient relaxation with adaptive line search.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports training on AdsTraj's 33,920 DFT structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates, with energy RMSE of 0.032 eV and force RMSE of 0.047 eV/Å.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen surface chemistries and environments requiring interactions beyond the local cutoff needs validation.
paper_title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction
